## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `finished_at` column needs fixing before merge. Its value is the `occurred_at` of a `started` event, so any process whose latest event is `started` shows that start time as its finish time. The documented NULL meaning is also wrong for processes that were started and then cleared. This review read the diff, `models/processes.sql`, `models/schema.yml` and the source table with its seed rows in `sources/process_events.sql`, and followed each seeded process through the new CASE expression. No tests were run.

## Changes
The pull request adds a `finished_at` column to the `processes` current-state model and documents it in `models/schema.yml`. It also adds a one-line `review.txt` file at the repository root.

## Critical
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — Stop deriving finished_at from 'started' events — Process 20, whose only event is `started` at `2026-01-01T00:01:00Z`, gets `finished_at = 2026-01-01T00:01:00Z` even though it has not finished. The expression `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end as finished_at` copies the start timestamp into the finish column. The source check constraint at `sources/process_events.sql:4` allows only `'created'`, `'started'` and `'cleared'`, so no finish event exists in the source to report. — Anyone reading `finished_at` will treat running processes as finished at the moment they started, which corrupts duration and completion metrics built on this model. — Fix: If the column is meant to hold the start time, rename it to `started_at` and update `models/schema.yml:9-11`. If it is meant to hold a finish time, the source needs an event type that marks completion before this column can be computed.

## Important
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — Correct the documented meaning of NULL finished_at — Process 30 (`started` at 00:02, then `cleared` at 00:03) gets NULL, but the docstring says "NULL means the process has never been started." The model keeps only the row where `recency = 1` (`models/processes.sql:12`), and the CASE returns NULL for every latest event other than `started`. That covers both `created` and `cleared`. — Consumers will wrongly conclude that cleared processes never started. This stays false even if you rename the column to `started_at`, because only the latest event feeds this column.
